author: hattrill
body: From [TCDB sub family 3.A.1.201](https://www.tcdb.org/search/result.php?tc=3.A.1.201) some of this family are mitochondrial. From my experience with ABC transporters, even members of the same subgroup can have very different substrates that differ from the archetypical member the group. i.e. predicting substrates can be tricky. Prob safer with mitochondrial prediction.

author: Antonialock
body: > > Does "H6TB12 transports acidic acylated and non-acylated sophorolipids (SLs) into the extracellular space", look strong? Well, in the paper they knocked out the transporter "MDR" H6TB12 (it doesnt appear to be involved in drug resistance) and sophorolipid secretion dropped to 10%. They also say the gene is located among other sophorolipid biosynthesis genes (ugta1, ugtb2, at, cyp52m1) https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/mmi.12200

author: hattrill
body: That looks convincing! So, defo not mitochondrial. Just an issue with ABCs being closely related but functionally diverse. Biosurfactants is not really a thing I have looked before. This paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8742932/ has a nice summary:

author: ValWood
body:
I think both are correct, the PAINT family is the issue
MDR is not the ortholog of the mitochondrial peptide-transporting ATPase which is conserved 1:1:1

I agree with Helen that its usually dangerous to infer substrates, but hte MDR branch appear to be a conserved role in exporting the peptides from processing.

MDR is in a different branch.
